title: Trump Pardons Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao Amid Reported Crypto-Ties Conflict Concerns
description_short: Trump pardoned Binance founder Changpeng Zhao on October 21, 2025; reports raised conflict concerns over crypto-business ties.
description_medium: The Justice Department records Donald Trump’s pardon of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao as dated October 21, 2025. Zhao pleaded guilty in November 2023 to failing to monitor money laundering at Binance and served a four-month sentence. Al Jazeera reported close dealings between Binance and the Trump family’s World Liberty Financial and said some viewed the pardon as a conflict of interest. Those reported ties raise concerns but do not establish that executives bought clemency.
description_long: The Justice Department’s clemency register lists President Donald Trump’s pardon of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao under October 21, 2025, and identifies the offense as failure to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program. The register lists a four-month prison sentence and a $50 million fine. Al Jazeera reported that Zhao pleaded guilty in November 2023 to one count of not monitoring money laundering at Binance and served a four-month sentence. The report also describes business ties between Binance and World Liberty Financial, the crypto company Trump and members of his family own: World Liberty launched its USD1 stablecoin on Binance’s blockchain in March 2025, and Binance promoted the coin. Al Jazeera says some viewed the pardon as a conflict of interest. The available records confirm the pardon and describe those business ties, but do not establish that the ties caused the clemency decision or that Zhao or executives bought it. The entry therefore records the pardon and reported conflict concern without presenting a quid pro quo as fact.

https://www.justice.gov/pardon/clemency-.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of the Pardon Attorney

supported_facts.quote: Zhao and Binance have been closely linked to the Trump family’s crypto companies. As such, the president’s decision to pardon Zhao is viewed by some as a conflict of interest.

supported_facts.quote: In March 2025, World Liberty Financial launched its own “stablecoin” – a dollar-pegged cryptocoin backed by US treasuries – called USD1. This was issued on Binance’s blockchain – a decentralised, digital ledger. In addition, Binance promoted USD1 to its 275 million users.

limitations: The report describes links and attributed concerns but does not establish that the ties caused the pardon or that clemency was purchased.
